topic: Statement and Assumption of Logical Reasoning
description: Statement and Assumption is a crucial topic in Logical Reasoning. An assumption is the implicit idea, premise, or belief that the speaker assumes to be true before making a statement.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Understanding the fundamental logical relationship between a given statement and its underlying assumption.

key_concepts.explanation: The information provided in the question that must be considered absolutely true while solving, even if it contradicts commonly known facts.
An idea that is not explicitly mentioned in the statement but serves as the core basis, motive, or underlying cause behind making that statement.

sections.title: Types of Valid Assumptions
sections.description: Rules for identifying and validating assumptions based on the specific nature and category of the statement.

results: People will read the advertisement/notice and pay attention to its contents.
There is an existing public demand or need for the product or service being advertised.
People will generally accept, listen to, and act upon the appeal or advice.
Issuing the appeal will result in a positive improvement or desired outcome in the current situation.
Citizens or the concerned targeted individuals will comply with and follow the rule.
The implementation of the rule is practically feasible and possible.

sections.title: Identification of Invalid Assumptions
sections.description: Understanding the scenarios and conditions where assumptions become logically invalid or completely flawed.

key_concepts.explanation: If an assumption contains extreme or definitive words like 'Only', 'Always', 'All', or 'Never', it is almost always considered invalid.
If an assumption merely repeats the exact words of the statement or acts as a direct paraphrase, it is not considered a valid implicit assumption.
An assumption that falls completely outside the scope and context of the statement, holding no direct logical connection to the core premise.

sections.title: Steps to Solve Questions
sections.description: A systematic, step-by-step guide to approach and accurately solve statement and assumption questions.

steps.title: Analyze the Statement
steps.detail: Read the statement very carefully and restrict your thinking strictly to the provided information. Do not apply your external general knowledge or personal biases.

steps.title: Understand Speaker's Perspective
steps.detail: Put yourself in the shoes of the speaker or author and think about the primary objective or purpose behind delivering this specific statement.

steps.title: Test the Assumptions
steps.detail: Evaluate each assumption individually to check if it provides a solid logical foundation for the statement. If the statement naturally follows from the assumption, it is implicit.

steps.title: Apply Elimination Method
steps.detail: Quickly eliminate options that contain extreme definitive words, are mere restatements, or introduce completely unrelated out-of-context ideas.
